concept: Prompt-format mirroring and structural priming in output
summary: Source-anchored research for Prompt-format mirroring and structural priming in output. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Language models show structural priming: they reuse recently seen syntactic structures, including when prime and target share no lexical overlap, indicating abstract structural representations. (high confidence)

Practical mitigation for instruction files: write the instruction file in the plain style wanted in the output (prose, little markdown) and state the desired format positively, rather than only listing prohibitions. (low confidence)

Anthropic's prompting guide says the formatting style of a prompt may influence Claude's response style, and that removing markdown from the prompt can reduce the volume of markdown in the output. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)

Prompt format alone can change measured performance a lot: up to 76 accuracy points on LLaMA-2-13B in few-shot settings, persisting with larger models, more shots, or instruction tuning; format performance correlates only weakly across models. (high confidence)
Format sensitivity falls with model strength: GPT-4 variants varied less across plain text, markdown, JSON and YAML than GPT-3.5-turbo, and no single format is best across models. (medium confidence)

A 2026 study (9,649 experiments, 11 models, YAML/markdown/JSON/TOON context) found no significant aggregate accuracy effect of context format (p=0.484), though individual models, mostly open-source, showed format-specific differences. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-01)
